page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-384GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 32 shared vCPUs and 32 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server exhibits poor single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, falling into the bottom 10%, and weak single-threaded gzip compression in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core and multi-threaded capabilities are significantly stronger. Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores both rank in the top 25%, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs in the top 25%. Most other metrics, including memory bandwidth, Passmark CPU and memory scores, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, fall within the average middle 50% range.

The shared CPU allocation presents a potential performance tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, predictable single-core execution. However, the high memory density of 384.0 GB relative to the 32 vCPUs offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive applications that do not constantly saturate individual CPU cores. This configuration is suitable for large-scale caching, memory-intensive database operations, multi-threaded text processing, and moderate-scale software compilation.
